Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services

merger_description:
Velocity I Purchaser, Inc. (an affiliate of various funds advised and/or managed by affiliates of Blackstone Inc.) (**Purchaser**) proposes to acquire 100% of the equity interests in FCH Intermediate Holdings, Inc and FCH Intermediate II Holdings, Inc (together, **Flow Control**) from FCH Preferred Issuer, L.P., minus rollover interests held by the Seller and Flow Control’s management (the **Acquisition**). The Purchaser will exercise sole control over Flow Control following the Proposed Transaction.

Flow Control is a US-based company that manufactures and supplies sanitary flow control solutions for the data centre cooling, food & beverage and pharmaceutical sectors. These products are primarily used to transport and control the flow of liquids in hygiene-sensitive industrial environments. Flow Control’s products include stainless steel weldment systems, fittings, tubes, pumps, valves, hoses, single-use assemblies, gaskets, and washdown equipment.

Flow Control has no subsidiaries, employees, assets or physical presence in Australia, but makes limited sales of its products to a small number of Australian customers primarily in the food & beverage and pharmaceutical sectors, through third-party distributors.

Blackstone is a US-based corporation, incorporated under the laws of Delaware, United States. Blackstone operates as an investment management firm.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given there is no horizontal overlap or
vertical relationships between Blackstone (and its connected
entities) and Flow Control in the supply of valves, fittings, hose
assemblies and washdown equipment.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
